source_admission: Published values used as constants or quoted ranges in industry.py and industry.md; no external dataset files are admitted. 'access' records how far each source was checked on 2026-10-09: 'full text' where the cited table or passage was read, 'abstract' where only the abstract was read, 'reported via search summary' where the value comes from a search engine's summary of the source and the source itself was not opened. The working digest is kept with the domain's run records on the research drive (resources-runs/industry_literature_digest.md). Bibliographic details of DOIs were checked against Crossref.

sources.citation: Krausmann, Wiedenhofer, Lauk, Haas, Tanikawa et al. 2017, PNAS 114, 1880-1885
sources.use: Global in-use stocks of 792 Pg in 2010; about half of each year's extraction builds or renews stocks; recycling supplies 12% of inflows to stocks; 335 t per person in industrial countries in 2010
sources.access: abstract (Europe PMC, PMC5338421); the 335 t per person reported via search summary, the publisher's full text being blocked

sources.citation: Velez-Henao & Pauliuk 2023, Environmental Science & Technology 57, 14206-14217
sources.use: Decent living standards need 32 t per person of direct and 11 t of indirect in-use stocks, 43 t in all, and a material footprint of 6 (3-14) t a year; buildings hold 98% of the direct stocks

sources.citation: Berglund-Brown, Dobie, Hewitt, De Wolf & Ochsendorf 2025, Buildings & Cities 6, 1099-1116
sources.use: Mean lifetime of about 15,000 demolished buildings: 81 years in nine US cities, 65 years in four European cities

sources.citation: UNEP International Resource Panel 2010, Metal Stocks in Society: Scientific Synthesis (lead author T. E. Graedel), ISBN 978-92-807-3082-1
sources.use: In-use stocks per person in more-developed countries: copper 140-300 kg, zinc 80-200 kg, aluminium 350-500 kg, iron 7,000-14,000 kg; copper lasts 25-40 years in a building

sources.citation: UNEP International Resource Panel 2011, Recycling Rates of Metals: A Status Report (Graedel, Allwood, Birat, Buchert, Hageluken, Reck, Sibley & Sonnemann)
sources.use: Only 18 metals, copper, zinc, aluminium, iron and titanium among them, pass 50% end-of-life recycling; 34 elements stay below 1%
sources.access: reported via search summary (UNEP press release of May 2011)

sources.citation: USGS 2025, Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025: Copper (Flanagan)
sources.use: World mine production 23 Mt in 2024; reserves 980 Mt; identified resources 2.1 Gt including 0.6 Gt already produced, undiscovered 3.5 Gt; aluminium substitutes for copper in power cable and electrical equipment

sources.use: A shield of 4.5 t/m2 brings the cosmic-ray dose to 0.5 rem a year; Table 4-1(a), 10,000 people at 1 rpm: the torus needs 9.9 Mt of shielding and 150 kt of structure at half an atmosphere over 6.8e5 m2 of projected area, the cylinder 23.3 Mt, the dumbbell 33.5 Mt and the sphere 46.7 Mt of shielding
